theme: Maternal and child nutrition through SHG-led nutrition-sensitive livelihoods and convergence with ICDS and health services
working_title: Poshan Saathi: SHG-led Kitchen Gardens, Nutrition Counselling and ICDS Convergence for Mothers and Young Children in Murhu, Khunti

geography.coverage: 20 villages in Murhu block. Specific villages to be confirmed by the applicant, aligned with existing SHG presence and Anganwadi centre catchments.

target: Pregnant and lactating women and children under five in SHG member households: about 1,200 women across 20 villages. The number of children under five is to be established at baseline.
budget_ceiling: Rs. 1.4 Crore total over 2 years (about Rs. 70 lakh per year), as an indicative planning envelope
problem_focus: Poor dietary diversity and inadequate maternal and young-child feeding and care practices in tribal SHG households, alongside incomplete uptake of available ICDS and health entitlements. The proposal addresses household food access through nutri-kitchen gardens, feeding and care behaviours through community counselling, and service uptake through structured convergence with Anganwadi and health systems. All delivery runs through existing SHGs rather than parallel structures.
planned_activities: SHG and Village Organisation mobilisation and orientation: sensitising existing SHGs and their federations in the 20 villages, identifying pregnant and lactating women and households with children under five, and developing village-level nutrition action plans owned by SHGs.

Nutri-kitchen gardens: training SHG households on year-round, climate-resilient kitchen gardens using local and indigenous crops, millets, greens and fruit saplings; distributing seed and sapling kits; setting up village demonstration plots; promoting low-cost water management (e.g., greywater use) drawing on the organisation's climate-resilient agriculture model.

Community nutrition counselling: selecting and training women from SHGs as community nutrition resource persons, who run group sessions in SHG meetings, recipe and cooking demonstrations with locally available foods, and targeted home visits during pregnancy, lactation and the first 1,000 days.

Convergence with ICDS and health services: working with Anganwadi Workers, ASHAs and ANMs to strengthen uptake of Take-Home Ration, growth monitoring, antenatal and postnatal care, immunisation and relevant maternity entitlements; active participation in Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Days; linking SHG meetings to Anganwadi calendars.

Early identification and referral: supporting community-level growth monitoring alongside Anganwadi, tracking at-risk mothers and children, and facilitating referral of severely malnourished children to government nutrition and health facilities.

Capacity building of frontline and community actors: joint trainings and refresher sessions for SHG leaders, community nutrition resource persons, Anganwadi Workers and ASHAs; exposure visits; block-level convergence meetings with ICDS and health officials.
Monitoring, evaluation and learning: baseline and endline surveys, a simple household tracking system, periodic review with SHG federations and block officials, and documentation of learning.

Sustainability and handover: building SHG federation and Village Organisation ownership of kitchen-garden seed banks and nutrition counselling, and embedding convergence routines into existing government platforms by project end.

research_needs: Demographic profile of Khunti district and Murhu block: total population, Scheduled Tribe share and main tribal communities, number of villages and households, literacy (especially female literacy), and sex ratio. Sources: Census 2011, District Census Handbook Khunti, and more recent official estimates where available.

District maternal and child nutrition indicators for Khunti: stunting, wasting, underweight, and anaemia in children and in pregnant and non-pregnant women; minimum dietary diversity and adequate diet among children 6–23 months; exclusive breastfeeding; institutional delivery; ANC coverage. Sources: NFHS-5 district fact sheet, with trends against NFHS-4 and the Jharkhand state average.
Socioeconomic context of Murhu block: livelihoods and agricultural patterns, landholding, seasonal migration, poverty and food security indicators, and PDS coverage.

ICDS infrastructure and service delivery in Murhu: the ICDS project covering Murhu, number of Anganwadi centres, Take-Home Ration and supplementary nutrition delivery status, and growth monitoring practice under Poshan 2.0 / Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan Tracker.

Health system context in Murhu: health facilities (CHC, PHCs, sub-centres / Health and Wellness Centres), ASHA and ANM coverage, VHSND functioning, and the nearest Malnutrition Treatment Centre (MTC) for referrals.

Relevant central and state policies and schemes: Poshan Abhiyaan / Mission Poshan 2.0, Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana, Janani Suraksha Yojana, any Jharkhand state maternal or child nutrition schemes, Jharkhand millet initiatives, and state convergence guidance between ICDS, health and the SRLM.

JSLPS (Jharkhand State Livelihood Promotion Society) presence in Murhu: SHG and Village Organisation coverage, any existing nutri-garden, Poshan Vatika or food-nutrition-health-WASH (FNHW) interventions, and community cadres already in place. Needed for alignment and to avoid duplication.

Agro-climatic suitability for kitchen gardens in Khunti: rainfall pattern, soil types, water availability across seasons, climate risks (dry spells, erratic monsoon), and suitable local and indigenous crops, greens, millets and forest foods.
Sector evidence on nutrition-sensitive agriculture and homestead or kitchen gardens improving dietary diversity in India or comparable contexts.
Sector evidence on SHG- or women's-group-based nutrition behaviour change and participatory approaches in tribal eastern India.
Evidence and good practice on community-level convergence between SHGs, Anganwadi and health services in India.
Local access and implementation considerations in Murhu relevant to field operations, such as village connectivity and remoteness, to be established from official or credible sources only.
org_fit: This builds directly on EcoKheti's SHG-led livelihoods and nutrition project with 1,200 women in Khunti and Gumla, which reported improved dietary diversity in 60% of households. It also uses the organisation's climate-resilient agriculture practice for year-round kitchen gardens, and its stated values of women's agency and convergence with public systems.
format_notes: No external RFP or donor format is prescribed. A standard full proposal structure applies: background and need, problem analysis, objectives, theory of change, activities, implementation plan and timeline, convergence and sustainability strategy, MEL framework with logframe, risk management, organisational capacity, and detailed budget. It can be tailored once a donor is identified.
